newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Decision on Jones expected tonight.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Decision on Jones expected tonight.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Sept 30 - Auckland coach Graham Henry will decide after training tonight whether to play flanker Michael Jones in Friday's Ranfurly Shield rugby challenge against Waikato in Hamilton, NZPA reports.

Jones, who missed Auckland's last two NPC games because of suspected concussion, underwent an hour long neuro-psychometric test on Saturday morning and was passed fit by Auckland team doctor Graham Paterson and neurological specialist Dorothy Gronwall.

However his replacement, the promising Dylan Mika, has been in excellent form at blindside flanker leaving Henry coy after Saturday's 50-23 win over Otago. He said he would make that decision on whether to play Jones or Mika after the team train tonight.
Auckland turned in probably their best performance of the season to date in their six-tries-to-two win over a game Otago.
They led 21-6 at halftime and never once did they look like being headed off by Otago with both the backs and forwards combining superbly.
"It was more of an 80-minute effort than last week, but we do respect the Otago side because they are a very good team," captain Zinzan Brooke said.
"I think our guys were a little bit shocked to have beaten them by that many points."

He doesn't expect Auckland to exert the same dominance on Friday night though, agreeing with Otago coach Glenn Ross' assessment that Waikato are "the form team in the competition at the moment and the best equipped to take on Auckland."
Brooke believes Waikato have developed sufficiently to make Friday night's sellout game a balanced affair.
"It is going to be very difficult to beat Waikato down at Rugby Park," he said.
"I would say they are one of the in-form teams at the moment, they've been nurturing young players for the last couple of years.
"It is easier to challenge for the shield if you get the guys right on the button.
"But if you get a team that has a bit of mongrel in it and wants to hold onto it then it is definitely hard to get it away from them. And I think that they are that sort of team."
Brooke wants his team to take the same approach they did last year when they challenged and beat Canterbury for the shield.
"It is going to be important that everyone focused for the game at training on Monday and Wednesday night. Challenging for the shield itself will do a lot for the buildup," he said.
"You don't want to think about it too much, you just want to stay relaxed and approach it the way we did the Canterbury game last year.
